name: @helm/desktop
description: Helm's Electron shell: main process, preload, renderer.
//productName: Electron derives app.getName() - and therefore %APPDATA%\<name> - from this file. Without productName a scoped package name puts the database in %APPDATA%\@helm/desktop, creating a nested folder from the scope. electron-builder sets the same value for packaged builds.
author: Cole Taylor

scripts.//dev: Goes through scripts/run-dev.mjs, which gives the run a data directory of its own under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Helm\dev. Without that, productName: Helm resolves userData to %APPDATA%\Helm - the installed app's - and the two fight over one Chromium profile and one helm.db. --fresh starts with no database, which is the first-run state. A second `pnpm dev` gets its own directory rather than failing on a held helm.db.
scripts.//dev:live: The old behaviour: unpackaged, against %APPDATA%\Helm, sharing everything with the installed app. Kept because it is the only way to see the real database in a dev build, and it says so loudly on the console and on the status bar's mode chip. --watch is what makes the main process and preload reload too; without it electron-vite only gives the renderer HMR, and every main-process edit needs the app killed and restarted by hand.
scripts.typecheck: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json
scripts.//test:e2e: The end-to-end tests: the built app driven through Playwright, each test in a temporary world with a fake claude (docs/TESTING.md). Builds first, because they run against out/, and builds the sample plugin, which the plugin tests drive.
scripts.test:e2e: pnpm --filter @helm/sample-plugin build && electron-vite build && playwright test -c e2e
scripts.//fidelity: TUI fidelity inside xterm - C1 to C9, against the spike page rather than the app. Goes through run-isolated.mjs: without it, productName: Helm resolves userData to %APPDATA%\Helm, so the run shared a Chromium profile with the installed app somebody is working in and wrote its report and its nine screenshots into that app's data directory. --fresh because this page opens no database at all, so seeding a VACUUM INTO copy of the real one would be work with no reader. Spawns no claude sessions and touches no network, but it does drive the real clipboard: C5 and C7 write to it and leave it empty. Pass --only=C1,...,C9 to re-run one check.
scripts.//claude-check: The real claude CLI inside the spike page's terminal. A diagnostic tool, not a test. Isolated like fidelity, so it never shares a Chromium profile with the installed app.
scripts.//packaging-check: Packaging, first run and the personal-path audit, in three phases. Phase 1 audits this checkout for personal paths (having first planted one to prove the auditor catches it) and checks the CLI Helm would launch against an independent 'where.exe' read. Phase 2 is a second app started with PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR pointed at a temp directory - the app's own portable-mode mechanism used as isolation - so first run happens against an empty database and an absent .claude without touching the real ones: it adds plain folders, scaffolds a harness and launches a real session from it, exercises the repos: key, converts a folder in place, and points the version guard at a stub CLI reporting 9.9.9. Phase 3 builds the artefacts if they are missing and runs the portable exe from a path with spaces. It does NOT install anything: verifying the NSIS installer means removing the Helm on this machine, so that is a tool (verify:installer) and not a group here, and PKG-2 stands open in the report to say so. Pass --only=audit|cli|firstrun|harness|scan|version|package to re-run one group.
scripts.//verify:installer: DESTRUCTIVE, and run by name only. Installs the built NSIS package over the Helm installed on this machine, runs its selftest, and uninstalls it - leaving no installed Helm behind. Refuses without --yes, and refuses again if Helm is running unless --replace-running. Not reachable from any suite: Helm hosts Claude Code sessions, so ending it ends the work inside it.
scripts.//dist:win: Goes through scripts/dist-win.mjs rather than calling electron-builder directly. electron-builder resolves pnpm with which(), which prefers pnpm.EXE over pnpm.CMD on Windows; a stale standalone pnpm shadowing the managed one makes it either fail outright or - worse - fall back to the npm collector and silently produce artefacts with no app.asar.unpacked, which is an exe that cannot dlopen better-sqlite3. The wrapper checks the resolved pnpm answers the declared version and shims it for the child process if not.
scripts.//verify:artifact: Asserts a built exe actually carries app.asar.unpacked, by unwrapping the NSIS artefact and the app-64.7z nested inside it. Checking dist-app/win-unpacked instead would be checking electron-builder's scratch directory rather than the file a person downloads. With no arguments it checks every Helm-*.exe in dist-app; the release workflow names the two it is about to upload. Needs 7-Zip, which ships on the windows-latest runner image.
scripts.//icon: Draws build/icon.* and packs build/icon.ico. The .ico is committed, so this is not part of the build - run it when the artwork changes.

//electron: Pinned exactly, not a range. electron-builder downloads platform binaries for one specific release and refuses to guess which - a caret here fails the packaging step outright (electron-builder 26.15.3). It is also the right shape regardless: the packaged app must ship the runtime the drivers measured against.
